sentences.text: Flavonifractor plautii, formerly Eubacterium plautii, is a Gram-variable, strictly anaerobic bacillus that forms part of the human gut microbiome.
A metabolic modelling study describes Flavonifractor plautii as a prevalent gut commensal combining flavonoid degradation with production of the short-chain fatty acids butyrate and propionate.
In that model, simulations identified acetyl-CoA pathways as the preferred route for butyrate production, while propionate synthesis occurred mainly via the methylmalonyl-CoA pathway.
A narrative review of reported Flavonifractor plautii infections found most originated from the gastrointestinal tract, commonly presented as sepsis, and were isolated from blood cultures.
That review reported a wide range of comorbidities among these patients, with immunocompromised patients predominating.
